name: Allow the licdn media host so the resume fetch is not silently blocked
request: Allow the licdn media host so the resume fetch is not silently blocked
checks: npm run check passed end to end: typecheck, build, 421/421 tests, validate (31 build files, 4 React entry points, service-worker imports)

rule discipline followed: CLAUDE.md rule 5 amended in this same task before the manifest change, and both host assertions kept as exact deepEqual lists with an added origin-shape check; the forbidden-permission assertions were not touched
git diff --check passed; scope is manifest.json, applicants.js, the two test files and the rule; no secrets; the signed media URL is never logged - only host plus two path segments via safeHost()
NOT verified against live LinkedIn (rule 17): whether the fetch was in fact being blocked on the user's account is exactly what the new warning will now say, and has not yet been read from a live run
result: The resume document is served from licdn.com while the page rendering it is on linkedin.com - a different origin - and licdn was absent from host_permissions, so the two page-side credentialed fetches (resolveResumeDocumentUrl and fetchResumeBytes) were refused before the request left the page. The only trace was a descriptor: check-failed field nobody opens, which is exactly the silent failure that makes a download problem undiagnosable. Added media.licdn.com and static.licdn.com to host_permissions, and made the blocked case log the host (never the signed URL) plus the hint that this is what an every-applicant check-failed means. Rule 5 was amended FIRST to state that LinkedIn's own media CDN counts as LinkedIn and that nothing else may be added without amending it again; the two exact-list manifest assertions were then updated deliberately and strengthened with a LinkedIn-owned-origin pattern check, rather than weakened. The permissions list is unchanged and the denied list is still asserted.
